comment: It's been $9.99 since 2011, so honestly this is fair. Still cheaper than most of my other subscriptions.
Student plan going up a dollar hurts when you're already broke. Not a huge deal yet but it adds up.
Family plan at $16.99 for six accounts is still way cheaper per person than anything else. Not switching.
Raising the price and still no lossless? Tidal has had HiFi for years. I'm moving to Apple Music, they already include lossless.
Good, maybe artists will finally see some of this. Spotify still pays fractions of a cent per stream though.
I'm on the free tier so this doesn't affect me. Ads are still annoying but whatever.
Greedy. Third price hike in a few years and the app keeps getting worse. Cancelling today.
Duo going up $2 stings, but we'll stay. It's still less than two separate plans.
Honestly I mostly pay for the podcasts anyway, so the music price bump is the least of my spending on audio.
YouTube Music Premium is $10.99 too and includes music videos. Might just move over at this point.
We don't need six accounts anymore, so I'm dropping from Family to Individual. Can't justify the extra cost right now.
Everything went up. Netflix, Disney, groceries. A dollar a month is nothing in comparison.
Going to Apple Music. They already do lossless and I'm tired of paying more for compressed audio.
If the app keeps getting more expensive and more bloated, I'll be back to downloading stuff the old way.
Honestly fair. Spotify is still the best app for music discovery and they're investing in the product. Glad to see it.
The app is so bloated with podcasts and video now. Paying more for this is wild when the core experience keeps slipping.
Amazon Music Unlimited is already cheaper if you have Prime. Moving my library over this month.
The free tier still works for me. If this keeps going up I'll just go back to free and deal with the ads.
I'd love for this to actually reach the artists, but I doubt it. The label deals are where the money goes.
Didn't even know it was going up. I don't really care either way.
People complaining about $1 should look at what the labels charge Spotify. Inflation is real and this is overdue.
Done. Cancelling and going back to free. Not paying more for a service that's clearly chasing profit over users.
Student plan is $5.99 now. I'm graduating soon so it doesn't matter much to me either way.
Switching to Tidal for lossless. I'm done paying more for compressed audio on Spotify.
Feels about right. Spotify has been underpriced for years and this still beats most alternatives.
Annoying, but I'm not switching. My playlists and years of listening history are too valuable to leave.
